title: STARBUCKS — QUIET KITCHEN
lessons: The player learns that Starbucks accepts clean personal cups across cafe, drive-thru, and mobile orders and rewards members for using one.
The player already has Rewards Stars and sees that Green-level Stars can expire after six months unless qualifying activity extends them.

text: The player learns that Starbucks accepts clean personal cups across cafe, drive-thru, and mobile orders and rewards members for using one.

entry-first-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: I can mobile order with my own cup now?

entry-first-2.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: Cafe, drive-thru, or mobile order. Bring it clean.

entry-first-3.speaker: PLAYER
text: And Rewards gives me something for doing it?

entry-first-4.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: Extra Stars on the personal-cup transaction. The behavior is easier to repeat when the system remembers to reward it.

choice-first.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: What do you make of that?

choices.text: That makes a reusable cup easier to actually use.
The process still depends on me remembering and cleaning the cup.
I do not want sustainability turned into another loyalty mechanic.

first-1.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: Exactly. The useful part is making the better habit work in every ordering channel.

first-2.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: Correct. I cannot automate the cup being clean and in your hand.

first-3.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: Fair. The environmental benefit and the loyalty incentive are two different reasons.
The player already has Rewards Stars and sees that Green-level Stars can expire after six months unless qualifying activity extends them.

entry-return-1.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: Your Stars are not a savings account.

entry-return-2.speaker: PLAYER
text: That sentence means I am about to lose something.

entry-return-3.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: At Green status, Stars can expire after six months.

entry-return-4.speaker: PLAYER
text: And you are reminding me because you know I hate losing them.

entry-return-5.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: Qualifying activity can extend them. Gold or Reserve changes the expiration rules. You can decide what that reminder does to you.

choice-return.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: What do you make of that?

choices.text: A reminder helps me use what I already earned.
Expiration makes the reward feel like pressure to come back.
If points expire, I stop caring about points.

return-1.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: Then the reminder saved value you already earned.

return-2.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: That pressure is real. If the Stars expire, the reminder also gives you a reason to come back.

return-3.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: Then let them expire.

return-3-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: You know I hate that answer.

return-3-2.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: I know. That is why the reminder works.
